identity.description:
D8 budget: a turn budget per reviewer, and the design updates from issues 22, 23 and 28

Part "budget" of D8 (the third bullet), and the TICKETS.md entry "Design updates from issues 22, 23 and 28". The passes default and the paired measurement are not in this PR.

## Turn budget

- Each reviewer pass now has a turn budget of 150 turns (was 40).
- A repo sets the budget of one reviewer with `reviewers.<name>.max_turns` in `.pr-review/config.yaml`, an integer of 1 or more.
- The dollar cap of a reviewer query follows the budget: `REVIEWER_USD_PER_TURN` ($0.05) times the turn budget. That is $7.50 at the default (was a flat $2). A repo that buys depth with more turns gets a cap that permits them.
- The wall-clock limit of a reviewer pass also follows the budget: `REVIEWER_MS_PER_TURN` (10 s) times the turn budget. That is 25 minutes at the default (was 10 minutes).
- The run-level `token_ceiling` does not change. It stays the limit of a whole run. No other role changes.
- Worst case, before and after: one reviewer pass $2 → $7.50. The reviewer stage of one full-tier run with all built-in reviewers selected (9 passes) $18 → $67.50.

## Limit stops in the recorded runs

Before the default changed, I counted the reviewer passes that stopped at the 40-turn limit or the $2 cap. The count is 0 of 1,117 reviewer passes, over 158 run records: the `pr-review-records` branch and the local eval run records. The pass cost had a median of $0.09, a p99 of $1.35 and a maximum of $1.85. So the new default does not change the typical cost of a review. It raises only the worst case.

## Design updates (docs/design/high-level-design.md)

- Section 10, decision 18: one SDK `query()` for each reviewer pass is the dispatch mechanism. A subagent mode is a budget option for the deep reviewers, not a recall lever. Closes #22.
- Section 6: a trusted custom reviewer with Bash gets read-only git commands. Explicit deny rules block fetch, pull, checkout, switch and gh. The record lists every permission denial. The text says that the current build does not apply these rules yet. Closes #28.
- Section 3.6 and decision 10: the non-blocking cap stays until D4c measures it against real records. If it changes, it caps nits only. Issue #23 stays open.
- Sections 3.4, 4 and 5 name the turn budget.

## Checks

- `npm test` (1428 passed), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.
- The new tests fail at the red commit 2cc62c2 (5 failures).
- The version goes from 0.10.0 to 0.11.0.
- No eval run: the change raises a limit that no recorded pass reached.

findings.claim: `max_turns` has no upper bound. A value above about 214,748 makes `timeoutMs` larger than the 32-bit limit of setTimeout. Node then fires the timer at once, so the reviewer pass times out right away.
findings.suggested_fix: Put an upper bound on max_turns in the schema, or limit timeoutMs to 2_147_483_647.
findings.explanation: setTimeout treats any delay above 2^31-1 ms as 1 ms. A very large turn budget therefore aborts the pass at once instead of giving it more time.

first.rationale: The schema `max_turns: atLeast(1)` has no upper bound. `timeoutMs` is 10_000 × `maxTurns`, and `client.ts` passes it straight to `setTimeout`. A `max_turns` of 214749 or more would exceed 2^31-1 ms and fire the timer at once. Only a repo owner who sets an absurd value can trigger this, and that value would also give a huge dollar cap.

escalated.rationale: The finding is correct: the schema sets only a minimum of 1 for max_turns, and the product of 10_000 ms and max_turns goes straight into setTimeout. Any max_turns of 214749 or more is over 2^31-1 ms, so Node fires the timer at once and every pass times out. Only an absurd config value triggers this, and the failure shows up as a timeout, so it is a suggestion rather than a blocker.

final.rationale: The finding is correct: the schema sets only a minimum of 1 for max_turns, and the product of 10_000 ms and max_turns goes straight into setTimeout. Any max_turns of 214749 or more is over 2^31-1 ms, so Node fires the timer at once and every pass times out. Only an absurd config value triggers this, and the failure shows up as a timeout, so it is a suggestion rather than a blocker.
